findings.title: DEF-46 acceptance claims '5 passed' but its cited raw artifact records '4 passed'
findings.body: docs/audits/DEF-46/acceptance.md:28 states 'Observed result after the execution-scope repair: 5 passed. The raw result is raw/runtime-crawler-pytest.stdout', but that file's summary line is '4 passed, 2 warnings in 13.77s' (raw/runtime-crawler-pytest.stdout:12). At main the test file collects 5 tests and all 5 pass (verified by --collect-only and a run), so current behavior is sound, but the packet's claimed number is not corroborated by the artifact it cites — a fifth test was evidently added after the raw capture without regenerating it. Legacy pre-schema packets are not machine-validated, so this survived review.

findings.title: No P1 release-wide rollback procedure or versioned release manifest exists yet
findings.body: Every child packet has its own recovery/revert notes (DEF-41 release.md:65-71; DEF-42 manifest.json:20 + recovery/; DEF-43 'revert the two implementation commits together'; DEF-44/45/46/47/48/90 recovery.md), and DEF-48 recovery.md:13-19 covers the harness plus its stacked-branch base. But there is no composite P1 revert procedure (no ordering across the stacked children) and no versioned P1 release manifest with per-criterion PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN, artifact hashes, reviewer identity and recovery procedure as DEF-24 step 7 requires: docs/release/p1-release-checklist.md has no rollback section, and only DEF-23 (P0) has a release-manifest.json. Expected while DEF-24 is 'scheduled', but the gate cannot be marked Done until this artifact exists.

findings.title: Enabled-capability manifest is distributed across artifacts, not a single named manifest
findings.body: PRD §19.6 (prd-v3.md:681) requires each release to include 'an explicit input/output example, one successful case, one honest failure case, the enabled capability manifest and relevant test evidence'. In substance all exist: docs/audits/DEF-48/examples/batch/{bundle.json,outcomes.jsonl,report.md} contain explicit inputs/outputs, five successes, a duplicate-URL distinct snapshot, and an honest typed failure ('failure — failure: http_error', no source proof; report.md:69-80); DEF-48/packet.json:22-27 carries machine capability flags (graph/model/browser/network all false); docs/release/p1-release-checklist.md:43-53 explicitly lists disabled/deferred capabilities with milestones, S1-S8 define the enabled path, and lines 55-69 state unverified-claim boundaries. No single artifact named as the P1 enabled-capability manifest exists; the positive 'enabled' set must be assembled from the checklist plus the packet flags.

findings.title: Hunt/Doctor coverage is N/A-or-degraded for every child; disclosed, never promoted to PASS
findings.body: Across DEF-23, DEF-41..48 and DEF-90, pip3r Hunt probes a CLI (no Python route; 'no CLI probe target' / zero commands) and Doctor executes no Python tests; every packet records these as UNKNOWN/BLOCKED/DEGRADED/N-A and none relabels them PASS (e.g. DEF-41 release.md:59-60; DEF-105 scope-plan.md:47-55; DEF-48/DEF-90 validator limitation results: pre-doctor-hunt BLOCKED, post-doctor-hunt DEGRADED). This is a residual, honestly-disclosed tooling limitation of the whole P1 evidence base, compensated by test/runtime/consumer evidence; it should be carried into the DEF-24 release record as residual debt rather than closed silently. Additionally the only skipped test across the four packages is api tests/e2e/test_gate0_contract.py:24, env-gated with an explicit reason.
